chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man has a right/due against me, and he denies it to me, then he deposits money with me. Is it permissible for me to take what is my due from him? He said: 'No, this is treachery/breach of trust.'

key_terms.يَسْتَوْدِعُنِي: He deposits with me / entrusts to me

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on deducting a debt from a deposited trust if the debtor denies the debt?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that retaining a deposited trust to offset a disputed debt constitutes 'khiyanah' (treachery), as the trust and the debt are distinct legal entities. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving the integrity of *amanah* (trust) even when rights are owed, requiring the creditor to return the deposit in full while pursuing the debt through proper channels or mutual agreement.
